title: Anthropic built an inspection layer that lets enterprises block sensitive data before it reaches Claude
excerpt: Inference hooks lets security teams inspect every prompt and tool call before Claude processes them. Works with Netskope, Palo Alto, Zscaler. One config covers all Claude products.
content_html:
TL;DR

Anthropic launched inference hooks for Claude Enterprise. Every prompt and tool call response passes through the customer’s DLP server before reaching Claude. Works with Netskope, Palo Alto, Zscaler. Covers all Claude surfaces with one config.

Anthropic launched inference hooks for Claude Enterprise, a system that routes every prompt and tool call through a customer’s own security server before Claude processes anything. The company’s DLP server inspects the content and returns an allow or deny verdict. Claude only proceeds once it has one. The same check runs on tool calls: when Claude calls a tool through MCP, skills, or plugins, the tool’s response is checked before it reaches the model.

The feature solves a specific enterprise problem. Security teams require every channel where employees can move sensitive data to pass through an inspection point they control. Until now, inline enforcement was limited to Claude Code’s client-side hooks. Inference hooks extends that to every Claude Enterprise surface, including chat, Claude Code, Cowork, and connected tools, with a single configuration at the organisation level. No separate integration per product.

The system uses a webhook-based protocol with a published schema, designed to plug into existing DLP infrastructure from Netskope, Palo Alto Networks, Proofpoint, Zscaler, or custom-built servers. Shadow mode (always allow) lets teams monitor before enforcing. Role-based exclusions and percentage-based rollouts let organisations phase in gradually. The White House is asserting control over who accesses frontier models, and inference hooks is Anthropic’s answer to the enterprise equivalent: letting companies control what their own employees send to the model.

The feature addresses the concern that Nadella and others have raised about enterprises “outsourcing their thinking” to AI providers. With inference hooks, Claude never sees the prompt if the company’s security server blocks it. The data stays inside the enterprise perimeter. Startups are raising hundreds of millions to build AI security control layers, and Anthropic is building that control layer directly into Claude rather than leaving it to third parties. Available in beta today for Claude Enterprise customers.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

Anthropic 为 Claude Enterprise 推出了推理钩子。 每个提示和工具调用响应都会经过客户的 DLP 服务器，然后到达 Claude。 与 Netskope、帕洛阿尔托、Zscaler 合作。 用一种配置覆盖所有 Claude 曲面。

Anthropic 为 Claude Enterprise 推出了推理钩子，这是一个在 Claude 处理任何内容之前通过客户自己的安全服务器路由每个提示和工具调用的系统。 该公司的 DLP 服务器检查内容并返回允许或拒绝的判决。 克劳德只有在有了一个之后才会继续。 对工具调用也进行相同的检查：当 Claude 通过 MCP、技能或插件调用工具时，会在工具的响应到达模型之前对其进行检查。

该功能解决了特定的企业问题。 安全团队需要员工可以移动敏感数据的每个通道，以通过他们控制的检查点。 到目前为止，内联执行仅限于 Claude Code 的客户端挂钩。 推理挂钩将其扩展到每个 Claude Enterprise 界面，包括聊天、Claude Code、Cowork 和连接工具，并在组织级别进行单一配置。 每个产品没有单独的集成。

该系统使用基于 Webhook 的协议和已发布的架构，旨在插入 Netskope、Palo Alto Networks、Proofpoint、Zscaler 或定制服务器的现有 DLP 基础设施。 影子模式（始终允许）允许团队在执行之前进行监控。 基于角色的排除和基于百分比的推出让组织逐步参与。 白宫声称控制谁访问前沿模型，而推理钩子是 Anthropic 对企业等价物的回答：让公司控制自己的员工发送给模型的内容。

该功能解决了纳德拉等人对企业“将思维外包”给人工智能提供商的担忧。 有了推理钩子，如果公司的安全服务器阻止了克劳德，他就永远不会看到提示。 数据保留在企业范围内。 初创公司正在筹集数亿美元来构建人工智能安全控制层，而 Anthropic 正在将该控制层直接构建到 Claude 中，而不是将其留给第三方。 今天为 Claude Enterprise 客户提供测试版。
